entry.dc:title: Optimization software for haulage in surface mining operations
entry.dc:creator: Bourgine B.
entry.dc:description: Loading and transport represent quite often the bulk of the extraction cost of surface mining. It is therefore essential to optimize these two operations. For this purpose, this article presents an interactive software of computation which can be utilized to calculate the size of a fleet of vehicles, i.e. to check the performance of a given fleet and to determine the optimum job assignments of the equipment. The architecture of this software is first explained. This is followed by emphasizing some of its features. In particular, the software effects a simulation of the operations of loading and of transport, and a calculation of the haulage times, based on the performance curves of the trucks. The program also makes use of a data base of the plant. An example is presented for the application of the program.

entry.dc:title: 420 t large-sized hydraulic mining excavator
entry.dc:creator: Ueda S.
entry.prism:publicationName: R and D Research and Development Kobe Steel Engineering Reports
entry.dc:description: Surface Mining Equipment for Coal Technology Research Association of Japan has recently developed the world's largest class of hydraulic mining excavator. Adopting a full array of electronic controls in the engines and hydraulic circuits, it attains smooth and precise semi-automatic control of the front attachment plus low energy consumption. Also equipped with HST swing circuit, fuel saving engines, one-piece crawler shoes, truck adjusters, an operation management system and other features on its fully analyzed frames, the machine is working successully in an Australian coal mine.

entry.dc:title: OVERBURDEN SPREADERS-LAYOUT CRITERIA AS FUNCTION OF OPERATIONAL CONDITIONS.
entry.dc:creator: Benecke K.J.
entry.dc:description: In surface mining, waste handling systems with continuous operation mode are composed of different handling devices. They form a chain with the spreader (stacker) as the final link. The paper deals with the dependence of spreader design and operational conditions. A spreader places waste in final location in high and deep dumps. The overall dump height decides the spreader geometry. This refers to both the receiving and discharge conveyor length. Stability and inclination of the dump slopes play a part, too. Handling rate and mobility are further design criteria. Crawlers are today's standard for the main undercarriage, best suited to poor traction conditions and bearing capacity prevailing on dumped waste. Tripper car and feeding conveyor support are subjected to operation mode, mobility and handling rate in their design, too.

entry.dc:title: Lead zinc mining industry - an overview
entry.dc:creator: Paliwal H.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: Considerable progress has been made in the growth of India's lead-zinc mining industry during the last one and half decades towards self-reliance. Developments in the coming years are likely to be more visible in the surface mining sector. Concerted efforts are required to indigenously innovate and develop appropriate technologies to match local needs, with selective import to keep pace with the mining world. This paper makes an attempt to give an overview of the status and prospects of lead-zinc mining industry and discusses demand and supply of the metals, resource position, growth profile, status of technology and thrust areas for future growth.

entry.dc:title: Geotama goes for gold in Indonesia
entry.dc:creator: Hayes D.
entry.dc:description: The firm's drilling program involves the use of the Longyear 38 rig for continuous coring for geological mapping. This helps establish the general viability of surface mining in any particular area. Two types of diamond bits are used to obtain core samples on the Longyear 38. Surface-set bits are used for the softer upper layers, while impregnated bits are employed for harder rock formations often found at greater depths. The Longyear rig has a 50 h.p. motor. It is designed for variable drilling speeds to cope with varying rock conditions and different drill bit sizes that need to be used. Most core drilling at the Cimas Concession has been between 400 to 800 r.p.m. For deeper drilling, Geotama uses a NQ surface-set bit. The 76 mm O.D. and 47 mm I.D. bit is hand set with five layers of diamonds ranging from 10/15 to 90/110 s.p.c. The step setting for each layer is 1 mm wide and 1.5 mm high with the top 'cutting' ridge 7 mm wide. The exact number of diamonds used and the spacing between them depends on the rock conditions at various sites. Once the Longyear drilling team locates a site of gold ore bodies, Geotama switches to reverse circulation drilling using a G & K 850 multipurpose rig.

entry.dc:title: Deformation of the facial skull of wild boar (Sus scrofa scrofa L.) as a possible result of Rhinitis atrophicans
entry.dc:creator: Lutz W.
entry.dc:description: In the forest station of Rheinbraun in the bituminous coal surface mining region of Northrhine-Westfalia one sow age 8-10 years and two wild boar piglets ages 8-10 months, each with a lateral deviation of the snout were shot during the years 1983, 1984, and 1987. The three skeletonized skulls were examined and the pathological changes were described. (compare figure). As possible causes of the deformations, Campylognathy, abscesses of the upper jaw, osteopathy due to mineral deficiencies, and Rhinitis were discussed. The pathological deformations of the three skulls correspond to the symptoms for Rhinitis atrophicans. The susceptibility of wild boar to this disease has been proven. A sure diagnosis can be made on the basis of evidence of the causal bacteria, Pasteurella multocida, and Bordetella bronchiseptica, as well as upon examination of the condition of the nasal cavities and nasal septa. © 1988 Verlag Paul Parey.

entry.dc:title: COMPUTER-ASSISTED MINE PRODUCTION PLANNING.
entry.dc:creator: Hendry J.W.
entry.dc:description: This paper will discuss the application of tools and the evolution of computer-assisted procedures in the production planning process at Quintette Coal Limited (QCL). In 1986 QLC produced 5. 3 Mt of clean coal from their surface mining operation located in northern British Columbia. The structural complexity of the sedimentary deposit and high rate of mining necessitate the consideration of large amounts of geological information which continually updates the interpretation. There are multiple unit operations required during the process of mining through a given multi-seam sequence, which results in many interdependent faces, and multiple iterations of scheduling sequences in order to satisfy a given set of objectives. In order to facilitate these activities in a timely fashion, it was recognized that a computer systems' capability needed to be developed which could increase the efficiency of information input, manipulation and output.

entry.dc:title: Evolutionary or fragmented environmental policy making? coal, power, and agriculture in the Hunter Valley, Australia
entry.dc:creator: Day D.G.
entry.dc:description: Intensified surface mining, power generation, and smelting operations in the Hunter River lowlands, NSW, Australia have posed numerous new environmental management problems. Legislative controls over water, soils, and land use management have been clearly insufficient and remain so. The complex range of environmental changes is challenging government agencies as well as coal developers. While water demands are increasing in the region the proportionally greatest competitors are power generation and irrigation. Comprehensive regional water quality assessment is inadequate and divided between a number of agencies with fragmentary interests. Coal development inquiries signal further controversy over appropriate management solutions and are an ongoing phenomenon in the region. The early 1980s resource boom has been followed by lower rates of economic growth, which have resulted in disparate agency responses to major ongoing environmental questions. While issue attention cycles are often remarkably short in environmental management, matters of water, land, and air quality require intensive and ongoing monitoring and policy development. © 1988 Springer-Verlag New York Inc.

entry.dc:title: OPTIMISING SURFACE MINING PRODUCTIVITY.
entry.dc:creator: Singhal R.
entry.dc:description: This paper provides general guidelines for selecting loading and hauling equipment and deals with scrapers, cable shovels, hydraulic shovels, front-end loaders, off-highway trucks and belt conveyors. Reference has also been made to mobile crushing systems. The concept of a 'match-factor' is discussed and its significance in relation to equipment utilization is highlighted. Bucketwheel excavation and draglines are excluded from this presentation.

entry.dc:title: NEW AND INNOVATIVE DEVELOPMENTS IN SURFACE MINING TECHNOLOGY.
entry.dc:creator: Atkinson T.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: In surface mining, most of the day-to-day management functions are conducted in the face of uncertainty. Equipment is usually subject to a difficult environment, and the nature of the deposit generally provides an imponderable unknown to other industries. These factors make it difficult to prepare reliable plans, and it is often difficult to detect whether any departure from an agreed plan is an appropriate response to unforeseen circumstances. It is in this area that management science, through the use of computer techniques, gives the possibility of providing management with better data for decision making, e. g. by simulation, use of probability distributions, etc.

entry.dc:title: Pulmonary function in silicosis
entry.dc:creator: Moore E.
entry.dc:description: The relationship between ILO Category for pneumoconiosis, spirometry and four indices of accumulated dust exposure was studied in the work force of an iron ore surface mining and beneficiation plant in Labrador. A significant difference (p < 0.05) in%PFEVand%PFVC was found between Categories 2, 3 compared with controls (Category 0) matched for all four indices: cumulative respirable dust (CD), peak respirable dust (PD), cumulative respirable quartz (CQ) and peak respirable quartz (PQ). There was no difference between ILO Categories 0 and 1 except for% PFEV, in PD. These findings support the view that simple silicosis is associated with decrements in lung function in addition to that which can be attributed to dust exposure. © 1988 The British Occupational Hygiene Society.

entry.dc:title: Bureaucratic Morality in the United States
entry.dc:creator: Rohr J.A.
entry.dc:description: This paper argues that the responsible use of administrative discretion is the most fundamental ethical issue for American bureaucrats; more fundamental than such highly visible issues as conflict of interest and financial disclosure. The argument is supported by references to academic literature, examples in administrative practice, and an analysis of the purpose behind the establishment of the Senior Executive Service in the Civil Service Reform Act of 1978. Although the responsible use of administrative discretion is not a problem confined to the United States, the formal separation of powers in the American Constitution gives the problem a peculiarly American orientation. Despite managerial doctrines on “unity of command,” American bureaucrats receive conflicting “signals” from competing institutions of government. This problem does not stem from misconduct on the part of anyone, but from the primary legitimating symbol of American politics, the Constitution of the United States. Specific examples of this problem are given from such areas as the EPA Superfund, passive restraints in automobiles and surface mining regulations. © 1988, Sage Publications. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Evaluating the effect of rock parameters on surface mine blasting by finite element analysis
entry.dc:creator: Sunu M.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: The blasting process in surface mines involves extremely complex interactions. Utilizing Finite Element (FE) analysis, the effect of rock mass properties and discontinuity data can be fairly idealized and assessed. The purpose of this paper is to present the application of finite element methods to fragmentation due to blasting in surface mining operations. As a result, the prediction and extent of blasting will help the engineers engaged in surface mining and construction operations to use explosives efficiently. © 1988, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Oil sands tailings sludge solidification and bitumen recovery
entry.dc:creator: Joshi R.C.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: Canada is a forerunner in the development of oil sands mining and processing technology. At present two commercial plants, both of them surface mining operations are producing approximately 200,000 of syncrude per day. At both of these plants a hot water separation process is used. The vast amounts of tailings, consisting of bitumen, sand, fines and water, generated from the hot water extraction process while recovering bitumen during surface mining operation, must be stored within gigantic man-made reservoirs created by constructing high dykes or dams. In this study, the potential of lime addition for stabilization of the sludge and recovery of bitumen has been investigated. Results of study indicate that more than 50 percent water as well as the bitumen can be recovered from sludge by centrifuging alone. With lapse of time, lime addition causes solidification of sludge as reflected by strength increase of treated and mompacted sludge. The implication of this investigation is that bitumen recovery from sludge is possible with the possibility of direct feed to the upgrading plant. The process discussed in this paper is economically measible. This is particularly true in those areas where bitumen recovery by surface mining is relatively high due to a high waste/ore ratio and when quality of mined oil sands is relatively low. © 1988, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Geotechnical and mine planning considerations in structurally thickened coal deposits at Smoky River Coal Limited, Alberta
entry.dc:creator: Dawson R.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: Structurally thickened coal deposits often form attractive surface mining targets. At Smoky River Coal Limited (SReL), economic occurrences of structurally thickened coal are found in folded and faulted strata due to the mechanisms of hinge zone dilation and imbricate thrusting (duplexes) respectively. The characteristic features of these steeply dipping and complexly structured deposits require that special attention be given to pit wall design and operational practices. This paper examines the characteristics of structurally thickened coal deposits at SRCL that affect the Burface mining process and explains relevant geotechnical parameters and operational considerations that are used to mine these deposits. Three case histories are also examined to illustrate design and monitoring rethods that are employed. © 1988, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Sedimentation ponds: A review of United States regulations affecting design
entry.dc:creator: Albert E.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: This paper discusses the surface mining regulations from four different states that directly affect the design, construction, and size of sedimentation ponds. Those states include Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Virginia, and West Virginia. The differences and similarities between various sedimentation pond design parameters will be discussed. © 1988, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Simulation of truck haulage systems in surface mines
entry.dc:creator: Maran J.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: Computer simulation can be used as a means of experimentation and evaluation of both truck allocation and dispatching problems especially when analytical methods are not suitable. The simulation language known as Q-GERT is introduced and evaluated in terms of its applicability to the modeling of surface mining activities. Through the analysis of a wide variety of situations, the program is proven to be an accurate modeling method. © 1988, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Federal administration of the surface mining control and reclamation act of 1977 in Oklahoma
entry.dc:creator: Vestal T.M.
entry.dc:description: SMCRA, which established detailed standards for the surface mining of coal, attempted to balance the need to increase coal production with safeguarding the environment. The act was based on the principle of cooperative federalism. The states were offered both positive and negative inducements to assume important roles in the design and implementation of regulatory programs consistent with the SMCRA. Oklahomas Department of Mines (DOM) carried out the provisions of the act so poorly that the federal Office of Surface Mining (OSM) was compelled to take over SMCRA inspection and enforcement. Other provisions of the act were administered by DOM, which found itself in a condition of "cohabitation" with OSM from 1984-1987. During that time, DOM became a stronger, technologically sophisticated agency; OSM gained a greater appreciation of the difficulties of implementing a state program; the mining industry became reconciled to reclamation contemporaneous with mining; and there was an increase in citizen participation. The return of primacy to Oklahoma may usher in a new federal relationship in surface mining regulation, with more power shifting to the states as budget pressures reduce funds and the number of employees in OSM. © 1988, CSF Associates, Philadelphia.

entry.dc:title: Pneumoconiosis in iron ore surface mining in labrador
entry.dc:creator: Martin J.R.
entry.dc:description: A cross-sectional survey of the work force at an iron ore surface mine and beneficiation plant in Labrador identified cases with a radiologic diagnosis compatible with simple pneumoconiosis by the International Labour Organization (ILO) classification (1980). Their distribution by ILO categories 1, 8, and 3, after excluding those with confounding diagnoses for pneumoconiosis, was 30, 10, and 2 cases, respectively. ILO category was related to age, duration of current employment, andcumulative respirable dust and quartz levels, as well as to decrement in ventilatory function. © by American Occupational Medical Association.

entry.dc:title: Natural aggregates of the conterminous United States
entry.dc:creator: Langer W.
entry.dc:description: Natural aggregates are widely distributed throughout the US in a variety of geological environments. Sand and gravel deposits commonly are the results of the weathering of bedrock and subsequent transportation and deposition. Crushed stone aggregates are derived from a wide variety of parent bedrock materials. Limestone and other carbonates account for approximately three quarters of the rocks used for crushed stone, with granite and other igneous rocks making up the bulk of the remainder. Some areas are devoid of sand and gravel, and potential sources of crushed stone may be covered with sufficient unconsolidated material to make surface mining impractical. In areas where suitable natural aggregate is not available or accessible, it may become necessary to improve the quality of existing aggregate, to import aggregate from outside the area, or to substitute artificial aggregate for natural aggregate. This report also discusses the aggregate industry in general terms, including exploration, mining, and processing, as well as aggregate production rates. -from Author

entry.dc:title: Zoological studies in recultivation areas of the Borken/Nordhessen lignite surface mining
entry.dc:creator: Aue N.
entry.dc:description: Epigaeic arthropods were examined from acidic brown coal areas of different recultivation. Important primary decomposers (Isopoda, Diplopoda) played no role even in the older areas. The macroinvertebrates of recently formed acidic ponds in the same area were investigated. The chemical analysis displayed extremely low pH, high conductivity, and a high concentration of toxic aluminium. Among the 12 indigenous arthropod species chironomids were dominant both in emergence and benthos. -from English summary
